hints: b and c only ever appear as b − c (−6b + 6c and 3b − 3c). Call u = b − c.
Now you have two equations in a and u. Solve them, then 2a + 3b − 3c = 2a + 3u.
1.why:
a − 6u = 4 and 6a + 3u = 50. From the first, a = 4 + 6u. Substituting: 24 + 39u = 50, so u = 2/3 and a = 8.

2a + 3u = 16 + 2 = 18.

hints: Multiply the independent choices: sandwich type, bread and size.
"Up to 2 of 6 sauces" means 0, 1 or 2 sauces. Count each case and add.
2.why:
Type × bread × size = 5 × 4 × 2 = 40.

Sauces: none (1) + one (6) + two (C(6,2) = 15) = 22.

40 × 22 = 880. 840 is what you get if you forget the no-sauce option (40 × 21).

hints: With base 1/4 (less than 1), log > 0 means the argument is between 0 and 1.
Solve n<sup>2</sup> − 7n + 11 < 1 for integers, then check each one is also above 0.
3.why:
n2 − 7n + 10 < 0 means 2 < n < 5, so n = 3 or 4.

But for n = 3 and n = 4, n2 − 7n + 11 = −1, which is negative, so the log isn't even defined.

So there are 0 such integers. The trap is answering 2 without checking the argument is positive.

hints: 1 + 3 + ... + 57 has 29 terms and adds up to 29<sup>2</sup> = 841. The sum of the first m odd numbers is m<sup>2</sup>.
If k is the (m + 1)th odd number, k = 2m + 1, the numbers below k add to m<sup>2</sup> and those above add to 841 − m<sup>2</sup> − k.
Remove the square digits 1, 4 and 9. You're left with 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, of which 2, 3, 5, 7 are prime.
Exactly one prime means the other two digits must be 6 and 8. Make the smallest such number.
5.why:
The digits are {p, 6, 8} with p prime. The smallest choice is p = 2, giving N = 268.

268 = 22 × 67, so it has (2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 6 factors.

hints: Between 3 years and 6.5 years the amount grows by 5040, so simple interest is 1440 a year. Work back to the principal.
Half-yearly compounding at r% a year means r/2 % per half-year, for 4 half-years.
If the roots are integers r and s, then r + s = 5 and rs = k.
k must be non-negative, so list pairs of non-negative integers that add to 5.
7.why:
Pairs (0, 5), (1, 4), (2, 3) give k = 0, 4, 6.

A negative root would make k negative, which isn't allowed. So there are 3 values.

hints: The minimum of x<sup>2</sup> + bx + c is at x = −b/2. Find min f and max g in terms of c.
Set min f > max g. You get a quadratic inequality in c.
8.why:
min f (at x = 2c) = 8c − 4c2. max g (at x = 3c/2) = 9c2/4 − 2c.

8c − 4c2 > 9c2/4 − 2c gives 25c2 < 40c, so 0 < c < 1.6.

Of the options, only 1/2 fits.

hints: Track litres of acid, not percentages. Start with 60 litres in 200.
Replacing with water multiplies acid by what's kept. Replacing with acid keeps 90% of the acid and adds 20 litres.
9.why:
After the first step: 60 × 0.8 = 48 litres.

Second: 48 × 0.9 + 20 = 63.2 litres. Third: 63.2 × 0.85 = 53.72 litres.

53.72 / 200 ≈ 26.9%, nearest to 27.

hints: Part 1: 960 m/min for 30 min = 28.8 km in 0.5 h, so speed 57.6 km/h. The four times are in AP and add to 3 h.
Times: 0.5, 0.5 + d, 0.5 + 2d, 0.5 + 3d with 2 + 6d = 3. Then write the total distance with speeds 57.6 + e, 57.6 + 2e, 57.6 + 3e.
Let the shifts be 13k and 9k. After 21 move: (13k − 21)/(9k + 21) = 19/14.
Then new students join as 3j and 8j. Set the new ratio to 5 : 4.
CP = CQ (both radii), so ∠PQC = 45° makes triangle PCQ right-angled at C. Find PQ and its distance from C.
The chords are on opposite sides of C. Use the 3 : 2 ratio to place SR, find its length, then use the trapezium area formula.
12.why:
PQ = 6√2 × √2 = 12, at distance 6 from C. So SR is at distance 4 on the other side.

Half of SR = √(72 − 16) = √56 = 2√14, so SR = 4√14. The chords are 6 + 4 = 10 apart.

Area = ½ (12 + 4√14) × 10 = 60 + 20√14 = 20(3 + √14).

hints: In parallelogram PQRS, the diagonals bisect each other, so S = P + R − Q.
Find the line through S and Q, then set y = 0.
60% of girls stay and 40% of boys stay: 0.6g = 0.4b + 8.
Both 0.6g and 0.4b must be whole numbers, so g and b are multiples of 5. Try b = 15, 20, 25, ...
14.why:
3g = 2b + 40, so g = (2b + 40)/3.

b = 15 and b = 20 don't give whole g. b = 25 gives g = 30, a multiple of 5.

Minimum total = 25 + 30 = 55.

hints: Area of a rhombus = d<sub>1</sub>d<sub>2</sub>/2, so d<sub>1</sub>d<sub>2</sub> = 792.
The diagonals bisect at right angles, so (d<sub>1</sub>/2)<sup>2</sup> + (d<sub>2</sub>/2)<sup>2</sup> = 36<sup>2</sup>. Then use (d<sub>1</sub> − d<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup>.
13 chairs cost 1300. A 26% profit means the customer pays 1638.
That 1638 is the discounted price of 12 chairs. The discounted price is 78% of the marked price.
Fix y, starting at 3, and count the x that are bigger than y with x + y ≤ 13.
The count drops by 2 each time y goes up by 1.
Compare the cost of the whole job for each worker: days × daily charge.
Use the cheapest worker as much as the 10-day limit allows, then the next cheapest for the rest.
18.why:
Whole job: Arun 24 × 2160 = 51840, Varun 21 × 2400 = 50400, Tarun 15 × 2160 = 32400. Tarun is cheapest, but alone he needs 15 days.

Tarun works all 10 days (2/3 of the job, 21600). Varun, next cheapest, does the last 1/3 in exactly 7 days (16800).

Total = 38400.

hints: Write both sides as powers of 3. The left side is 3 to the power 1<sup>2</sup> + 2<sup>2</sup> + ... + 20<sup>2</sup>.
The right side is 3 to the power 21 + 22 + ... + (20 + m). Compare the exponents.
19.why:
Left exponent: 20 × 21 × 41/6 = 2870. Right exponent: 20m + m(m + 1)/2.

m = 57 gives 1140 + 1653 = 2793, too small. m = 58 gives 1160 + 1711 = 2871, just over.

m = 58.

hints: 10 shares of A are worth 1200, so B and C together are worth 2100.
Let B = b shares and C = 20 − b. Write the value equation.
Let gold = G. Bonds = 0.25G and stocks = 100000 − 1.25G.
Total gain: 10% of stocks + 6% of bonds + 8% of gold = 8200.
Split by [x]. For [x] = 3 you need [x<sup>2</sup>] = 9, that is 9 ≤ x<sup>2</sup> < 10.
Do the same for [x] = 4 and 5, and check x = 6. Watch the endpoints: √10 itself gives [x<sup>2</sup>] = 10.
22.why:
S = [3, √10) ∪ [4, √17) ∪ [5, √26) ∪ {6}.

Options B and C include √10, where [x2] = 10 ≠ 9, so they fail. Option A includes numbers up to √18, beyond √17.

Option D, (3, √10) ∪ [5, √26) ∪ {6}, sits inside S, so it's a possible subset.
